Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from German Sekunde, in turn from Latin secunda.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sɛˈkundɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -undɐ
  • Syllabification(key): се‧кун‧да

Noun

[edit]

секу́нда • (sekúnda) f

  1. second (unit of time)
  2. (figurative) moment

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
секунда
Wikipedia ru

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin secunda, feminine singular of secundus; ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sekʷ-.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sʲɪˈkundə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

секу́нда • (sekúnda) f inan (genitive секу́нды, nominative plural секу́нды, genitive plural секу́нд, relational adjective секу́ндный, diminutive секу́ндочка)

  1. second (unit of time)
    високо́сная секу́нда, секу́нда координа́ции ― visokósnaja sekúnda, sekúnda koordinácii ― leap second
    • (Can we date this quote?), “(Please provide the song title)”, in Семнадцать мгновений весны [Seventeen Moments of Spring]:
      Не ду́май о секу́ндах свысока́
      Ne dúmaj o sekúndax svysoká
      Don’t look down upon seconds
  2. A second (unit of angle)
    углова́я секу́нда ― uglovája sekúnda ― second of arc, arcsecond
  3. A second (musical interval)
    большая секу́нда ― bolʹšaja sekúnda ― major second
    ма́лая секу́нда ― málaja sekúnda ― minor second
  4. (figuratively) a short amount of time
    подожди́ секу́нду ― podoždí sekúndu ― wait a moment
    сию́ секу́нду ― sijú sekúndu ― just a moment
